title: Reconcile README badges and eval claims with tracked eval evidence
description:
## Problem

Current tracked evidence contradicts the README. README badges/table/Eval Status claim "51/51 improved" and average final-pass score 95.50, but eval/results.tsv has latest scored rows for only 10 agents and docs/eval/scorecard.md reports "Agents with eval rows: 10" and "Average latest score: 80.97". This is the highest-priority gap because it is a public trust claim. Decide explicitly whether to complete the missing eval evidence or revise public claims to the truthful current state; do not leave both versions in the repo.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read README.md badges/table and Eval Status.
2. Read docs/eval/scorecard.md.
3. Summarize eval/results.tsv latest rows by agent.
4. Observe README says 51/51 improved and 95.50 average, while scorecard/results show 10 agents and 80.97 average.

## Evidence From Reality Check

node summary of eval/results.tsv returned rows=19, latest_agents=10, scored=10, improved=10, avg_post=80.97. docs/eval/scorecard.md independently reports Agents with eval rows: 10 and Average latest score: 80.97.
acceptance_criteria: README, docs/eval/scorecard.md, docs/eval/scorecard.json, release notes, badges, package metadata, and eval/results.tsv are mutually consistent. If only 10 agents are currently evidenced, public copy says that plainly. If the intended claim remains 51/51, eval/results.tsv contains valid latest rows for all 51 agents and the generated scorecard proves it. CI/npm test fails if the README eval badge/summary drifts from generated scorecard data.
close_reason: Reconciled stale README eval badge/table/section with scorecard/results evidence and added drift gate; scorecard claims validator passed.

title: Reality check: close Healthcare Agents product-proof gaps
description:
Reality-check evidence from 2026-05-30:
- README promises 51 specialist healthcare administration agents, 10 domains, multi-runtime installation, CLI discovery/routing, trust/safety boundaries, and eval quality controls.
- agents/registry.json and agents/*.md currently line up at 51 agents; local CLI list/choose/doctor smoke probes work.
- npm test completed successfully and covers shell syntax, prompt lint, heuristic audit, npm pack dry-run, CLI help/list, and installer --all dry-run.
- eval/results.tsv has 19 rows, 10 latest scored agents, 10 improved agents, average post score 80.97.
- docs/eval/scorecard.md also says only 10 agents have eval rows and average latest score is 80.97.
- README badge and Eval Status section claim 51/51 improved and average final-pass score 95.50, which current tracked evidence contradicts.
- npm pack --dry-run includes scripts/__pycache__/audit-agents.cpython-312.pyc because package.json includes scripts/ wholesale; ignored Python bytecode is currently shipped if present in the working tree.
- .beads had 7 total issues, all closed, covering old eval documentation cleanup only. No open bead covered current product-proof gaps.
- br and bv were not available in this runtime; bd is the healthy repo-local bead CLI.

This epic is the bridge from the documented v1.3 product vision to a release state that is truthful, reproducible, and hard to regress. The work is not to add random polish; it is to make every major README/release claim either (a) proven by tracked evidence and automated gates, or (b) rewritten so users are not misled.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed with evidence. README, release notes, scorecard, registry, package contents, CLI behavior, installer behavior, and eval coverage agree with one another. CI/npm test fails on the specific drifts found in the reality check. No remaining core README promise is unsupported by either implementation or explicit limitation text.
notes:
Plan-space refinement notes:
1. Initial beads covered the hard evidence gaps: false eval/README claim, missing scorecard gates, weak CLI/installer/package proof, untracked docs/extracted, and lack of bead coverage.
2. Ambition round added longer-term trust infrastructure: source freshness, public artifact verification, scenario canaries, routing metrics, and release manifest traceability.
3. Refinement added tracker-tooling documentation, a registry generation/update contract, and installer/CLI security checks.
4. bd dep cycles reports no dependency cycles. bd ready currently lists the epic itself because bd parent-child links are structural; bd refused making this task child block the epic ("epics can only block other epics"). Treat beads-i70.12 and beads-i70.17 as the terminal closure gates for the epic in practice.
close_reason: All 20 child beads are closed with current validation evidence. README/release claims now match scorecard/results, release gates prevent drift, package/CLI/installer/safety/source/routing/manifest checks pass, and tracker coverage is documented.

title: Harden npm package contents and exclude ignored/generated artifacts
description:
## Problem

npm pack --dry-run currently includes scripts/__pycache__/audit-agents.cpython-312.pyc because package.json includes scripts/ wholesale and the pycache exists in the working tree. That means ignored/generated Python bytecode can leak into the published tarball. Package contents should be deterministic and limited to source, docs, eval kit, and intended assets.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure scripts/__pycache__/audit-agents.cpython-312.pyc exists after running the Python audit.
2. Run npm pack --dry-run.
3. Inspect Tarball Contents.
4. Observe scripts/__pycache__/audit-agents.cpython-312.pyc listed even though .gitignore ignores __pycache__/ and *.py[cod].

## Evidence From Reality Check

npm pack --dry-run listed scripts/__pycache__/audit-agents.cpython-312.pyc in the tarball. git status did not show it because it is ignored, so the package files list is broader than the intended source-controlled release surface.
acceptance_criteria: Package configuration excludes __pycache__, *.pyc, test caches, temp artifacts, local run logs except README, and untracked/generated junk. Add a packlist validation test that inspects npm pack --json or tarball contents and fails on forbidden patterns. A clean npm pack dry-run no longer includes scripts/__pycache__ or any ignored bytecode.
close_reason: Hardened package files list and added packlist forbidden-pattern validation; node scripts/validate-packlist.js passed and excludes docs/extracted and __pycache__/pyc.

title: Add pinned offline source and fixture cache for Operator OS
description:
What: Add pinned source snapshots/metadata and fixture caches so Operator OS release checks can run without live external fetches.

Why: Live source fetching with retries improves currentness, but it makes tests and release checks slower and more failure-prone. A deterministic cache gives maintainers reproducible evidence and a fallback when agencies, public datasets, or MCP tools are temporarily unavailable.

Pros: deterministic CI, faster release checks, reproducible evidence, safer debugging.
Cons: requires cache refresh workflow, storage conventions, and stale-cache warnings.
Context: During /plan-ceo-review for Healthcare Operator OS, live fetches with retries were chosen for initial implementation. Preserve this as future hardening once the first live research path and case fixture schema exist.
Effort: M human -> S with CC+gstack.
Priority: P2.
Depends on: initial live research fetch implementation and case fixture schema.
acceptance_criteria: Release checks can run from pinned source metadata and fixture caches without live network fetches; live refresh is an explicit command; stale-cache warnings are documented and tested.

title: Triage untracked docs/extracted health-system-research tree
description:
## Decision Needed

The current worktree has an untracked docs/extracted/ tree containing a health-system-research README and several agent prompts. It is not part of tracked package files and was not touched during this reality check. Decide whether it is intentional product scope, source material to import, generated scratch output to ignore, or stale local state to remove outside this branch.

## Rationale

Untracked documentation can confuse reality checks and release preparation: it may represent intended product scope that is missing from package/docs, or unrelated local extraction output that should not influence release claims. The decision should happen explicitly because the tree sits under docs/ and looks product-like.

## Alternatives Considered

1. Commit it as part of the product docs, with README navigation and package.json files coverage.
2. Ignore it as generated/local extraction output.
3. Move it to the correct project if it belongs to a separate health-system-research pack.
4. Remove it after owner confirmation if it is stale scratch output.

## Evidence From Reality Check

git status showed ?? docs/extracted/. rg --files listed docs/extracted/README.md and health-system-research agent files. npm pack --dry-run did not include docs/extracted because package.json files only include specific docs subtrees.
acceptance_criteria: There is an explicit decision recorded and implemented: either the tree is committed with docs/navigation/package intent, ignored as generated/local extraction, moved to the correct project, or removed by the owner. The package/files config and README do not accidentally omit intended docs or accidentally ship unintended extracted content.
close_reason: Decided docs/extracted is local extraction scratch outside packaged product scope; added docs/extracted/ to .gitignore and packlist gate proves it does not ship.
